title: Service package version manifest (manifest.json) — contract v1
description: One version of one service, as data. Lives at packages/<category>/<service>/versions/<version>/manifest.json in stackvo/stackvo-service-packages. This file is what replaces the six compile-time tables the app used to carry (template.rs DYNAMIC_SERVICES, config.rs EMBEDDED, commands.rs RENDERED, connect.rs SPECS, migrate.rs, env.schema.json serviceDependencies) — see docs/servis-market-mimarisi.md §3.2. Everything the app needs to install, render, connect to and remove one service instance is here, and nothing else is.

apiVersion.description: The manifest contract this file speaks. The app declares a supported range and refuses anything outside it — a package written for v2 must not be half-read by a v1 client.

service.description: Service id, lowercase. Must equal the containing <service> directory name. Becomes part of every derived name: instance slug, container name, volume name, compose key, compose profile.

version.description: CONCRETE version. Must equal the containing <version> directory name. A moving tag is forbidden here (ADR 0014): a manifest whose image can change under it has no fixed digest, so it cannot take a place in the hash chain that makes an installed package verifiable. 'latest' is expressed at registry level as the `recommended` flag, and migration resolves it to a concrete version before writing instances.json.

registry.description: Registry host. Present because not everything is on the Hub — Elasticsearch and Kibana come from docker.elastic.co, which has its own token handshake. Checked against policy.market.allowedRegistries before a pull is proposed.

repository.description: Repository path without the registry host and without the tag. Official images are bare ('mysql'); the Hub resolves them under library/.

tag.description: The FULL tag, not the version. These differ more often than they look: RabbitMQ 4.3 is pulled as `4.3-management` because the plain tag exists for series the management one does not, and verifying the bare name would pass while the pull failed (examples/service_tags.rs found this).

digest.description: Optional but strongly preferred. With it, the image is pinned and 'the same version' means the same bytes. Without it, the tag can move under the user. tools/probe-tags.mjs resolves and records these.

capabilities.description: What this service can be USED as, independent of its id — 'sql', 'cache', 'search', 'smtp', 'object-store'. This is what a settings entry of type instanceRef matches against, so phpMyAdmin can say 'point me at something that speaks sql' rather than naming mysql and being wrong when the user runs mariadb.

multiple.description: May more than one version of this service run at once? False for anything bound to a single subdomain (the admin UIs) or a single host resource — a second instance would collide on a name no allocator owns. The app must not guess this: a wrong guess is either a refused install or two containers fighting over one domain.

identity.description: What distinguishes two instances of the same service. Only 'version' in v1 — named instances ('mysql-shop', 'mysql-crm') are a v2 question and the field exists so that answering it is not a schema break.

name.description: Stable handle used by the compose template as {{ port.<name> }} and by instances.json. Names, not positions, because a port added in the middle must not renumber the rest.

container.description: The port inside the container. Fixed by the image; no allocation touches it.

preferred.description: The host port to try first. A single-instance user gets exactly the number they have today; ports.rs only moves on when it is taken. Replaces both of the old key families (HOST_PORT_<ID> and SERVICE_<ID>_HOST_PORT) — 31 template variables in two spellings, 17 of which had no default anywhere and so could not be changed from the UI at all.

legacyKey.description: The .env key this port was read from before packages existed, for migration only. Present because the mapping is not derivable in reverse: `HOST_PORT_MAILPIT_SMTP` and `SERVICE_MINIO_CONSOLE_HOST_PORT` both reduce to a handle, and reconstructing the key from the handle would have to guess which of the two families a service used — which is exactly the guess C-09 records the cost of. A migration that guesses wrong does not fail; it silently reallocates a port the user's tooling already has written down.

primary.description: The port a connection string is built from. At most one per manifest.

name.description: Handle, not the Docker volume name. The real name is derived per instance (stackvo-<instance>-<name>), which is the whole point: 18 templates hardcode a single volume name today, so two versions of one service would share a data directory and the newer one would upgrade the older one's datadir irreversibly.

purgeable.description: May `market_uninstall --purgeData` delete this? ADR 0012 moved data deletion out of disable and into uninstall; this field is what the deletion reads, instead of the regex over template text that discard_service uses today.

files.description: Config files rendered beside the compose fragment and bind-mounted in. Replaces commands.rs's RENDERED/COPIED tables — which, measured today, name a percona/my.cnf that does not exist in the tree and silently renders nothing.

name.description: Handle used by the compose template as {{ file.<name> }}.

template.description: Path inside the package, always under files/. No traversal, no absolute paths — the unpacker rejects anything else before it writes a byte.

mode.description: Octal mode the rendered file is written with. Read-only by default: it is generated output, and a user who edits it in place loses the edit on the next render (ADR 0002).

sha256.description: Of the template as shipped, so a client can tell the file it downloaded from a file somebody changed.

settings.description: What a user may configure, and the ONLY things a compose template may interpolate. This is a security boundary, not a convenience list: the render context is built from this array, so a downloaded template cannot reach the rest of the user's .env and write it into an environment: line.

key.description: Bare key, without the SERVICE_<ID>_ prefix the old .env family carried. Used as {{ settings.<KEY> }}.

type.description: 'secret' routes the value to the OS keystore (ADR 0010) and masks it with config::MASK everywhere it crosses IPC. 'instanceRef' names another instance rather than a literal, which is how an admin UI points at a database without hardcoding a container name.

default.description: For type=secret this is a first-boot default (e.g. 'root'), written into the keystore at install and expected to be changed. A real credential here is a CI failure — CONFLICTS.md C-18 is the previous round of that mistake.

required.description: Refuse to install until this has a value. For the setting a service genuinely cannot start without, not for the one with a sensible default.

options.description: For type=enum. An offer, not a constraint, on the same terms as the version combobox.

capability.description: For type=instanceRef: which capability the referenced instance must have. 'primary' as a default value means 'whichever instance currently holds the legacy alias'.

label.description: Locale → human label. Absent means the app falls back to the key.

connection.description: How to build a connection string for this service, or null for one you open in a browser instead (the admin UIs). Replaces connect.rs's compiled SPECS table. Both addresses come from here — the host one (127.0.0.1 + allocated port) and the container one (instance alias + container port) — because a service has two and picking either as 'the' connection string is where the confusion started.

scheme.description: URI scheme, or one of the non-URI forms: 'host-port' for drivers that take a contact point (Cassandra), 'smtp' for mail catchers.

port.description: Which entry of ports[] the string is built from, by name.

defaultUser.description: The account the image itself creates, used when userSetting is unset or empty.

passwordSetting.description: settings[] key holding the password. Its value never reaches the manifest — the keystore holds it and the string is assembled at read time.

databaseSetting.description: settings[] key naming the database the string points at.

defaultDatabase.description: The database the image creates on first boot whether or not anyone configured it.

options.description: Query parameters the string needs to actually work — Mongo's authSource=admin is the one that fails silently without it.

url.description: Web-facing services only: the Traefik subdomain. Null for anything you reach with a client rather than a browser. Note this is the field that forces instancing.multiple=false today — two instances would want one name, and per-instance subdomains are a separate, smaller job.

subdomain.description: The label in front of DEFAULT_TLD_SUFFIX — 'phpmyadmin' becomes phpmyadmin.stackvo.loc.

port.description: ports[] entry the router forwards to, by name.

test.description: Compose's healthcheck test, verbatim. Written as a list because the string form is run through a shell.

interval.description: How often to ask, as a Compose duration ('10s').

timeout.description: How long one check may take before it counts as a failure.

retries.description: Consecutive failures before the container is called unhealthy.

startPeriod.description: Grace period during which a failure does not count — a database that takes a minute to initialise is not unhealthy, it is starting.

dependsOn.description: What this service needs to be useful. Replaces env.schema.json's serviceDependencies block, which its own note admits is 3 entries out of 20 and references a service that does not exist (C-16). A package declaring its own dependency is the only version of this that cannot go stale.

capability.description: Matched against other packages' capabilities[], not against a service id — 'sql' rather than 'mysql', so mariadb satisfies it too.

service.description: Optional narrowing when only one specific service will do (Kafbat genuinely needs Kafka, not any queue).

required.description: True when the service cannot function without it, false when it merely works better. Required is what blocks an install; optional is what suggests one.

companions.description: Extra containers this service cannot run without, which are NOT independently installable — Kafka's Zookeeper is the only one in the current catalog. They are named per instance like the main container, so two Kafka instances get two Zookeepers rather than fighting over one.

name.description: Handle for the companion, and the suffix of its derived container name — a Kafka instance's Zookeeper is stackvo-<instance>-zookeeper.

file.description: The compose fragment, at the package root. ONE service, no top-level services:/volumes: keys — which is what removes template.rs's 80-line awk imitation, whose whole job was re-indenting standalone compose files back into fragments.

sha256.description: Of the fragment as shipped. Checked on every read, not only at install: the point of writing a hash down is to catch the change nobody announced.

support.description: ADR 0014. 'Supported' must be a measurement, not an opinion: tools/eol.mjs checks this block against endoflife.date and a divergence fails the PR. Note that an eol version is still PUBLISHED — a version that exists in somebody's .env today must have a package or their migration stops. Publishing and promoting are different things, and this field is the difference.

eolDate.description: When upstream support ends or ended, ISO date. Compared against endoflife.date by tools/eol.mjs rather than trusted.

source.description: Where the status was measured from, so the next reader can repeat the measurement instead of believing it.

notes.description: Locale → a sentence shown next to the version in the picker. For the thing that will otherwise be discovered from a stack trace: MySQL 5.7→8.0's authentication plugin change, Elasticsearch 7→8's security-on-by-default.
